title: Trim Letter Triples
statement:
You get a string s of lowercase letters. Delete as few characters as possible so that no letter appears three or more times in a row. Return the resulting string.

The result is unique: from every run of the same letter you must keep exactly min(run length, 2) copies, and it does not matter which copies you delete.

examples.why: The run "aaa" loses one a, the run "bbbb" loses two b's. Everything else stays.
Each run is cut to two. The two x-runs stay separate because the y's sit between them; nothing merges into a new triple.
Four a's in total, but never three next to each other, so nothing is deleted.

constraints: s contains only lowercase English letters
hints: Build the answer one character at a time. When is it unsafe to append the next character?
Appending c is only a problem if the last two characters of the answer so far are both c.
Keep the answer in an array (or track the current run length) and skip a character when it would be the third in a row. Join at the end.

explain.intuition:
Each run of one letter is independent: a run of length 5 must shrink to 2, a run of length 2 stays. So you just copy the string while refusing any character that would be the third copy in a row of the output.

That greedy choice is always safe, because a deletion inside one run never changes the runs around it: the next run starts with a different letter, so nothing can merge. The only subtle part is cost. Deleting characters from a string one at a time copies the string each time; build a new array and join it once.
steps: For each character c of s: if the last two entries of out are both c, skip it.
pitfalls: Comparing with the last two characters of the input instead of the output. In "aaaa" the fourth a would then be checked against the deleted third one.
Removing characters from the string inside a loop, which is O(n²) on a long run.
Cutting runs to one copy instead of two.

solutions.title: Delete one triple at a time
solutions.idea: Find any three equal letters in a row, delete one, and repeat until there are none.

solutions.title: Build the output, skip the third copy
solutions.idea: Append each character unless the output already ends with two copies of it.

followups: Allow at most k copies in a row instead of two.
Now each deletion has a cost per position. Keep at most two in a row while deleting the cheapest characters.
lcTitle: Delete Characters to Make Fancy String
